justifications.c1: No £ cost for a pellet-store run-out: only a £30-per-pallet missed-delivery charge (PelletCo, odd host) and unpriced emergency/Saturday surcharges (LC Energy, Maine Energy Systems, MB Energy); the file itself says the ~£500–£2k figure is unsourced.
justifications.c2: No run-out rate per site; the 828 lost hours at Grantown Primary (Press and Journal, search-confirmed) were boiler breakdowns blamed on slow spare parts, not empty stores; the weekly store check was not sourced.
justifications.c3: Workarounds exist (supplier low-level alarms such as Balcas DELOX, paddle switches, oil back-up boilers, combined maintenance-and-supply tenders) but no labour time or £ cost was found, and the Balcas evidence is a vendor listing.
justifications.c4: Ofgem RHI requires accurate biomass fuel records, with lost payments for inaccuracy (search-confirmed), but these are fuel quantity and sustainability records, not store-level monitoring; no insurer, CQC or school rule requires level monitoring (recorded not found).
justifications.c5: Councils run biomass school estates and procure pellets and maintenance by public tender (bidstats), which points to slow procurement; no job advert or role owning fuel supply was found, and Highland schools mostly burn chip, not pellets.
justifications.c6: Pellet suppliers already bundle level monitoring with delivery: Scandbio's level watcher with web portal and supplier-managed ordering (search-confirmed, Sweden) and Balcas sensors in UK/IE (vendor listing); VEGA targets supplier-managed silos. A strong channel, though UK evidence is thin and incumbents hold it.
justifications.c7: Willingness to pay is shown only in adjacent feed-silo monitoring (BinSentry $79 install + SaaS, Nanolike SEK 16,500 for 5 years, Halo $8,333); pellet-specific offers are unpriced and supplier-bundled, so the gap is asserted, not evidenced.
justifications.c8: NB-IoT silo monitors exist, but no component prices or BOM were gathered, the store is dusty, and possible ATEX/DSEAR zoning for an electronic sensor in combustible pellet dust was not checked.
justifications.c9: Comparable silo monitors charge subscriptions (BinSentry, Nanolike, Halo) and the reorder cycle repeats each season, but no source says level logs meet RHI record duties and no per-site subscription price for this niche was found.
justifications.c10: Regional press (breakdowns, not run-outs), a Highland Council briefing note on pellet supply problems, an Italian school closure and a US forum restart thread; no UK report of a site losing heat because its pellet store ran empty.

weakest: There is no sourced evidence that pellet stores actually run empty at UK sites or what one run-out costs, so both the pain and its size rest on assertion.
